items.title: Are Tariffs Making Prices Go Up?
items.summary: As Americans continue to worry about the cost of living, U.S. tariffs are back in the news. So we asked international trade economist and School of Global Policy and Strategy Dean Caroline Freund the question on many consumers' minds.

items.title: Why a Doctor Saying ‘It’s Normal’ Can Backfire
items.summary: Research shows that patients often interpret normalizing language to mean treatment isn’t necessary, but the misunderstanding can be prevented.

items.title: Mindfulness-Based Therapy for Opioid Misuse Offers Massive Return on Investment
items.summary: A mindfulness-based treatment for opioid use disorder could generate $12 in economic benefit for every dollar spent, a massive improvement on current approaches.

items.title: UC San Diego Launches New Business Data Science Major
items.summary: The first program of its kind in the UC system, a new bachelor’s degree from the Halıcıoğlu School for Data Science and Computing and the Rady School of Management will enable students to turn data into strategic business decisions.

items.title: Why Is the Toy Story Franchise so Successful?
items.summary: The fifth Toy Story installment recently surpassed over $1 billion at the box office making it the highest-grossing film of 2026. So what is the secret behind the franchise’s enduring appeal? Shawna Kidman, associate professor of communication explains why in this Q&A.

items.title: What Explains Gender Pay Gaps in Academia?
items.summary: A study of University of California social science faculty tested several common explanations and found that none told the full story.
